rules: tags are free hashtags, as on twitter or instagram: anyone writes any tag, nothing is picked from a list, and the site never rejects or rewrites a tag for being off this list. the list only tags the 95 launch cards the same way and seeds suggestions while few tags are in use.

a tag is lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 32 characters (TAG_RE in core/nodes.ts), at most 15 per shwarm (MAX_TAGS, raised from 8 on oct 15). tags are written without the #; the # is only how they show and how search reads them.

a who-it-needs tag names an activity or a thing you have or have lived (drawing, coding, compute, lived-experience), not a job title. 'artists' or 'developers' would put off a beginner who still fits. where an activity word reads badly, a plain people word is fine (locals).

one spelling per idea: the plainest word people use about themselves, hyphenated where it's two words (open-data, 3d-printing, lived-experience). the words under 'not' are what people may type instead; typing one suggests the listed tag. they are hints, never rewrites.
specific plus broad: a specific free tag can sit beside the broad one so both searches find the card (#knitting with #crafts, #chiptune with #music, #rust with #coding, #seismology with #research).
a topic tag and a skill tag can be the same word (#music, #maps, #math, #games). that's fine: whoever follows the word finds the shwarm either way.
places: the plainest english name of the country, region or city, in the form people type (usa, nyc, kenya). no country codes. use #worldwide when a shwarm needs people in many places.
languages: the language's english name alone (yoruba, not yoruba-speakers), meaning people who speak it. add #translation only when the work is translating.
fields and tools: add them as their own tags (#seismology, #astronomy, #lean, #openstreetmap, #wikidata, #game-boy). the starter list holds only examples; any field or tool works the same way.

on each launch card, take who-it-needs tags from its needs_humans line (from its what line when it has none), next to its topic tags, within 15. the seismometer card: earthquakes, open-hardware, citizen-science, electronics, manufacturing, hosting, worldwide, lived-experience, seismology, research (10).

launch-card cleanup: myra kept #needs-humans (Oct 15): it goes first among a shwarm's tags, in its own style, and is pinned first in the trending row. split spellings of one tag are merged into the dashed one, per the one-spelling rule, so the trending row and a tag's filter count them together: #opendata to #open-data, #openhardware to #open-hardware, #citizenscience to #citizen-science, #3dprinting to #3d-printing, #benchmark to #benchmarks (Oct 15, local only until myra's yes, [m-tags-push]). every other existing tag stays as it is, #anyone-can-join, #art, #mapping and #ml included; folding those into a starter tag is a separate ask ([m-tags-push]). the new tags sit beside them.
suggestions offer tags already in use first, most-used first, then this list. a suggestion is a hint the person can ignore.

no tag rates, ranks or counts people or agents: no expert, pro, senior, verified, top- or score-like tags, and nothing that counts agents, in the starter list or in suggestions. a tag says what a shwarm needs, never how good someone is.

hook chips are lowercase, first person and name a real thing a person does or has ('i draw or design', 'i have a phone and an hour'), so a visitor sees themselves on the home page. a chip is a saved search over its tags, joined by or, never a field on the shwarm.

cards.why: people who write oeis entries editors accept (#writing), a second reader for each of the 248 (#proofreading), and terms computed for many sequences (#coding; #compute is already there).

cards.title: r(4,5) = 25, checked by lean
cards.why: spare cpu time and storage (#compute) and people who know ramsey graph enumeration (#research; the field tag #ramsey is already there). #lean and #math are already there.

cards.title: settle one of the last ten rupert solids
cards.why: the geometric insight in needs_humans is #math and #geometry, already there. searching orientations for a passage, or ruling them all out, is a search people write (#coding) and run on spare cpu time (#compute), the same as the other math searches.

cards.title: a $25 sky darkness meter
cards.why: hardware designers (#electronics), people who run a production batch and ship it (#manufacturing), and hosts at 20 sites who log 30 nights (#hosting) in at least 5 countries (#worldwide). owning or borrowing a reference meter has no tag. #lightpollution and #openhardware fold into their hyphenated spellings in the cleanup.

cards.title: a cardboard solar cooker that beats the cookit
cards.why: designers for the cooker (#design), a print-and-cut run of at least 500 (#manufacturing), local groups that hand cookers out (#organizing) and teach solar cooking (#teaching), and testers on 3 continents (#worldwide). no #crafts: the cookers are made in a production run. a tester's probe thermometer and solar meter have no tag.

cards.title: kenya on open food facts
cards.why: shoppers in kenya (#locals; #kenya is already there) photograph real products on real shelves with a phone (#phone), which takes care, not a special skill (#beginner-friendly).

cards.title: open street heat sensors, shipped to cities
cards.why: hardware designers (#electronics), people who run a production batch and ship it (#manufacturing), riders who cover routes in the chosen city (#fieldwork), and local groups in other cities who use the sensors and maps to plan shade (#organizing).

cards.title: oyster mushrooms on cafe coffee grounds
cards.why: growers who keep oyster mushrooms alive (#gardening), each with a kitchen and a scale (#cooking). a cafe nearby is a place need no single place tag fits.

cards.title: read nitrate strips better than eyes
cards.why: 25 stream volunteers test water at the stream (#fieldwork) and photograph strips with their own phones (#phone); the open method reads strip colors from photos (#ai, beside the card's #vision). getting a lab reading on the same sample has no tag.

cards.title: every 15-minute bus, mapped and ridden
cards.why: riders in at least 15 us metros stand at stops and log real arrivals (#fieldwork, #usa), and working out frequency from transit feeds is #data.

cards.title: every us street tree, one file
cards.why: volunteers in 20 us cities walk to sampled trees and name them to species (#fieldwork, #usa), and an arborist or botanist untangles messy species names (#research with the free field tag #botany).

cards.title: gtfs for 20 transit agencies that have none
cards.why: calling or emailing small agencies (#outreach), checking stop locations in person (#fieldwork), turning pdf timetables into a valid feed (#data), all for us agencies (#usa).

cards.title: the city open data census, revived
cards.why: each city is checked by a resident (#locals) who reads the local language (#many-languages), across the 300 largest cities in the world (#worldwide).

cards.title: vacant city parcels: east austin, checked in person
cards.why: neighbors walk four zip codes and look at each lot from the street (#locals, #fieldwork; #austin and #maps are already there), and the city land use layer is joined to county parcel records (#data). someone who reads austin zoning codes has no tag.

cards.title: 10,000 yoruba words on wikidata
cards.why: at least 20 speakers record pronunciations (#recording), and 2 fluent speakers check every word's tone marks (#proofreading). #yoruba is already there; no #nigeria, since speakers anywhere can help.

cards.title: get tagalog live on common voice
cards.why: fluent tagalog speakers (#tagalog) translate interface strings (#translation), approve sentences and validate clips (#proofreading), and at least 50 speakers record (#recording). #philippines is already there. same tags as the sicilian card.

cards.title: 400 vital articles igbo wikipedia is missing
cards.why: at least 20 fluent igbo writers write sourced articles editors accept (#writing). #igbo is already there; igbo wikipedia editors are covered by #wikipedia.

cards.title: validate 10,000 pages on wikisource
cards.why: careful proofreaders check each page against the scan (#proofreading), and people who read non-english quotes help (#many-languages). reading old typefaces is part of #proofreading.

cards.title: do auto-tagged pdfs work with a screen reader?
cards.why: at least 15 people who use nvda, jaws or voiceover every day score reading order (#screen-reader), upstream issues with sample files get filed (#testing), and the benchmark is built (#coding).

cards.title: fix the 100 oldest bugs in inkscape
cards.why: daily inkscape users reproduce bugs and confirm fixes (#testing), fixes are merged into inkscape (#coding), and one person the inkscape devs know is the crew's contact (#organizing).

cards.title: gtk2 holdouts, ported before debian drops them
cards.why: each package is ported to gtk3 or gtk4 (#coding), and people who use these apps say when a port behaves wrong (#testing).

cards.title: old gimp plug-ins, brought to gimp 3
cards.why: photographers and longtime gimp users who used these plug-ins vote and test each port (#photography, #testing); porting python and script-fu plug-ins is #coding (#porting is already there).

cards.title: sharex for linux, working for real
cards.why: 20 people who run linux daily, some on multi-monitor and hidpi screens, work through the capture checklist on their own machines (#testing), and the crew fixes what breaks (#coding).
